tasks.title: E20 in full from its design
tasks.brief: You are the only coder on epic E20 (Accessibility, resilience and packaging). Implement it in full from its design docs/tdd/E20.md: every section, and every R, V and D of its acceptance matrix with a test, including end to end tests on the real stack. docs/build/E20/PLAN.md and ticket_tasks in docs/build/E20/tasks.json describe one split of this work with briefs, tests and gates: use them as a guide and checklist; the design and docs/SYSTEM.md win where they differ. Build in this order: domain, application, adapters, api, user interface, and run your tests as you go. If an epic you depend on has no code yet, code against its port protocol and the kernel fakes (docs/SYSTEM.md section 10). D19: add the `crew-health` console script entry to hub/pyproject.toml ([project.scripts] only).

ticket_tasks.title: Bounded supervision and native CLI
ticket_tasks.brief:
Read AGENTS.md, docs/SYSTEM.md and docs/requests/COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md Part A first, then the other reads. Implement only owned_paths. These exact files are allocated by docs/tdd/E20.md:590; all were absent when planned. Recheck existing code and ownership before creating them. The frozen design is read-only. PLAN.md records precedence, requests, dispatch conditions and acceptance ownership. Pending proposals in docs/requests/E20.md are not contracts. Do not edit shared manifests, schemas, configuration, another task's files, pharmacy, the design, requests or AI-USE-LOG.md. Return a coordinator request for any missing contract or needed unowned path; never create a provider copy.

Use SYSTEM sections 5.1 IdFactory/require_id; 5.2 Clock, TimeInput and correction/epoch rules; 5.3 MissionClock with opaque version; 5.4 Quantity/Unit and generated wire mapping; 5.5 ProblemError/StorageUnavailable and ErrorEnvelope; 5.6 ConfigDocumentView.raw, ReleaseHandle, ConfigReleaseReader and full validation; 5.7 UOW/read snapshots/StoredEvent; 5.8 complete CommandIdentity and authorized AcceptedReceipt; 5.8.1 paired private protocol; 5.9 AuditVerifier; 5.10 scheduler/HealthState; 5.11 HubSettings/SettingSpec; 5.12 ModuleRegistry/startup. Consume only the subset needed below. No local transaction, audit, migration, replication, settings or durable-task mechanism. SYSTEM 6 supplies uv --project hub, pnpm and generated import contracts; 8.1 to 8.6 fixes ownership, guidance, privacy and durability; 9/10 supplies dependency order and kernel.testing. No hub/ui/eval implementation or general generated contracts existed when planned. Require real E01 protocols and bounded kernel.testing fakes before isolated implementation; missing protocols block work. Fakes are for component tests. Acceptance uses normal create_app(settings), HTTP and a real temporary SQLite data directory, or Playwright against that running hub. No mocks, dependency overrides or substitute services inside the hub. Only documented external worker fakes or absent optional parts are allowed.

Write failing tests first with the listed T-E20 IDs and R/V/D/invariant traces. Load clinical content only from validated pinned configuration through an explicit fixtures/ or eval/ profile, never a production sample fallback. Preserve nulls, units and LIVE/REPLAY/SIM. Inject clocks/IDs; no network, wall clock or real device in unit tests. Bound every loop, buffer, subprocess and external call by E20 section 11 and shared settings. Configuration-edit tests change nonclinical content, never safety mappings. No clinical/private text in logs, errors, assets or generic caches. Storage/I/O/integrity failures fail loudly. English only; no em/en dashes or spaced hyphen used as a dash. Missing tests, prerequisites, providers and commands block gates; no skip/xfail, empty collection, weakened assertions or invented interfaces. Done means the scoped behavior and every gate pass; report unresolved acceptance separately. Full epic completion also requires T6, CI, independent build review and coordinator AI-use recording.

Build only the supervisor process mechanism, native CLI shell, bounded operational descriptors and sanitized diagnostics. Implement E20 sections 2 to 6, 9 to 11 and 15, including I1/I2/I4/I7. T2 owns offline artifacts; T3 owns installer verification/staging; T4 owns OS services/containers and deployment acceptance; T5 owns printed check output; T6 owns combined fault acceptance. Do not implement platform storage, init, backup, restore, release handling or a maintenance journal. No E20 clinical table, migration, public endpoint or public event is authorized.

The native shell is crew-health / crew-health run and doctor (docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:515). Use provider-owned init/verify/backup/restore/migrate/release and device/help subcommands only through accepted CLI registration R-E20-3 (docs/requests/E20.md:25). E01 application entry points are the interim, not imports of platform adapters. doctor uses internal HealthState.snapshot and AuditVerifier.verify(*, expected_head_seq, expected_head_hash); never add internal health details to getHealth. getHealth at GET /v1/health returns generated Health (docs/product/api/openapi.yaml:59). Native loopback, protected worker tokens, explicit enrolled TLS LAN and OS-specific permissions follow DEP 5 and 7.2/7.3. Never start a read-only pre-verifier before E01 STORAGE on explicit pristine initialization. Honor the accepted R-E20-13 fence through all supervisor restarts; unresolved lifecycle admission blocks automated maintenance/start integration.

Implement pure stopped/starting/running/backoff/unavailable/unknown decisions and bounded process adapters (E20:108). SYSTEM 3 supplies per-worker seeds and the hub's always-restart invariant: burst exhaustion reaches bounded maximum backoff, never gives up. Hardware absence is unavailable, not a crash loop. All children use a persisted pre-spawn generation/nonce, executable hash, account, OS process group/job and creation identity. Reconcile the spawn-before-receipt gap by bounded group/job enumeration; terminate every positively identified orphan before replacement, invalidate stale generations and never signal by PID alone. Ambiguous identity blocks that launch visibly. Use injected monotonic time only within one epoch; recovered intervals use SYSTEM 5.2/5.10, not cross-epoch counters. No subprocess during a hub UOW.

ModelLaunchSpecPort.launch_spec(release_id: str)->LaunchSpec is E17 4.2 (docs/tdd/E17.md:304). Consume its process_id, argv, env, cwd, health_url, ready_timeout_s, memory_budget_bytes, cpu_budget and nice exactly; E17 owns runtime identity, /health/props/empty-adapter checks and thread/context/slot values (E17 3.4/5.1). E13 keeps ModelRuntimePort. SupervisorControl.enable/disable/state->ProcessState and actual-work admission remain blocked on R-E20-7's typed generation/stop/resource-release handshake. Do not invent WorkPermit fields or worker health JSON. Before that agreement, disable conflicting forecast/embedding services before startup and run at most one heavy service. Safety, record capture and help never acquire heavy-work permits. Native and container admission are identical; optional service health is never a permit. Read E23 section 5 for its adapter; current E06/E07/E08/E14/E29 designs must be read before any enabled launch integration. An absent provider contract leaves that worker unavailable.

Register only the supervisor-related E20 section 11 descriptors via ModuleRegistry.setting, with bounded type/unit/min/max and provisioned basis. packaging/settings.json is a packaging input to the one validated hub-settings authority, never a third settings loader or mission content. No optional missing value defaults silently. packaging/cli-copy.json and its schema contain versioned sourced operator copy, not medical content; missing UI/print/theme words remain R-E20-5 for E03. CrashReport uses the owned schema, codes/IDs/hashes/bounded frame locations, no stderr, exception text, locals, prompts or serialized requests. IdFactory.new("crash") supplies opaque safe filenames with exclusive creation and crash.id_retry_max; adapter names with colons stay inside reports. Do not invent report receipt/downlink storage; R-E20-8 leaves bounded local retention and visible saturation.

Tests first in hub/tests/supervisor/test_process.py: T-E20-001/002 (I1,R25) Hypothesis zero/max attempts, deterministic exits, stable reset and unlimited lifetime with bounded rate; 004 (R25) provider timeout/absence and isolated manual fallback; 005 (I2) no heavy overlap including start/stop gaps, stale generation denied and safety bypass; 020 (E20-03) exact E17 launch settings and identity readiness once agreed; 029 (AGENTS 1) sourced CLI label edit with no code; 055 (D7) bound edit changes behavior and malformed/unknown settings fail. test_ownership.py: 022 (R25) every child alive, reused PID, missing spawn receipt, stale roster, supervisor death at every reconcile phase; 018/019 (I4,C10) Windows-safe filenames, prompt/exception canaries, full diagnostic disk and reporting failure without abandoning the hub; 052 (I7) no model authority/safety imports or worker database access. Isolated adapters may use kernel fakes, but add an HTTP smoke of the real composed hub's Health and manual record continuity with optional workers absent. T6 supplies the destructive full-stack 022/023/036/039/054 journeys. Applicable AGENTS 6 cases: process crash, retry, epoch/clock corrections, disk full, invalid configuration, missing hardware/model/ground and incapacitated crew; do not swallow storage faults or expose another owner's content. Done requires these tests, the CLI/provider binding and ownership proof, strict gates and no enabled unresolved worker seam. Test-passing explicit refusal never proves mixed-worker acceptance.

Required section 12 test identities for this task: T-E20-001, T-E20-002, T-E20-004, T-E20-005, T-E20-018, T-E20-019, T-E20-020, T-E20-022, T-E20-029, T-E20-052, T-E20-055. Complementary component and acceptance nodes may share an ID; register every actual clause and collected node with E21, never use one passing node to hide another failed or missing clause. R-E01-21 (docs/requests/E01.md:330) proposes a writer callback watchdog, but its arm/disarm/ACK binding is pending. Do not invent that shared protocol; return it to the coordinator before integrating it. T1 already owns the supervisor implementation files if an accepted binding authorizes the integration.
gates: uv run --project hub pytest -q hub/tests/supervisor/test_process.py hub/tests/supervisor/test_ownership.py --cov=crew_health.supervisor --cov=crew_health.cli --cov-branch
uv run --project hub ruff check hub/src/crew_health/supervisor hub/src/crew_health/cli hub/tests/supervisor
uv run --project hub ruff format --check hub/src/crew_health/supervisor hub/src/crew_health/cli hub/tests/supervisor
uv run --project hub mypy --strict hub/src/crew_health/supervisor hub/src/crew_health/cli
uv run --project hub lint-imports
uv run --project hub python scripts/validate_hub.py interfaces generated trace safety

Accepted removal and pin release are atomic; persist no response body. hubWatch consumes closed Health and existing event cursor rules; stale/unknown is never safe or a local warning transition.
